 JUDGMENT Lakshmamma vs Ganesh M.R on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146277636/
1

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Jayalakshmi V J who met with road traffic accident.

2. That on 05-12-2022 at about 07-00 p.m., when Jayalakshmi (hereinafter called the deceased) was standing on the left side of Bangalore-Kunigal road, near Brilliant Vyali School, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagar District,
at that time motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HS-7622 came from Bangalore main road in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased result of which the deceased sustained injuries.

Immediately the deceased was shifted to Manasvi Hospital,
Nelamangala, but the deceased was died on 06- 12-2022.

So far they have spent more than Rs.2,
00,000/- towards medical, transportation expenses and funeral obsequies expenses.
Deceased was aged about 25 years, she was doing a Tailoring work in Gokul Garments, Bangalore and thereby earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of deceased, petitioners have suffered pain and mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

3. The respondent No.1/ RC owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HS-7622 has filed written statement and contended that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and same was insured with the 2nd respondent and the policy was in force at the time of accident.
It is further contended that the rider of motorcycle was holding valid driving licence.
Hence, in the event if court comes to the conclusion that petitioners are entitled for compensation then respondent no.2 is liable to pay the compensation.
4. The respondent No.2/the Insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HS-7622 has filed written statement and contended that the offending vehicle was not at involved in the alleged accident.

It is further contended that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint, that the offending vehicle was falsely implicated by the petitioners by colluding with the owner of the vehicle and police to get the compensation from the respondent no.2.

It is further contended that the rider/owner of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and that the petitioners are not the legal representative of the deceased and they have no right to claim compensation for the death of deceased.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that, Smt. Jayalakshmi V J died on account of road traffic accident in 05-12-2022 at about 7-00 p.m., on Bangalore- Kunigal road, near Brilliant Vyali School, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagar District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HS- 7622?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?

Lakshmamma vs Ganesh M.R on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146277636/
2 3.
What Order or Award?
6. The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as Pw1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.10.
The respondents have not adduced any oral evidence.

7. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 9 Issues No.1:-

Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, the deceased Jayalakshmi (hereinafter called the deceased) was standing on the left side of Bangalore-Kunigal road, near Brilliant Vyali School, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagar District, at that time motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-HS-7622 came from Bangalore main road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased result of which the deceased sustained injuries.
Immediately the deceased was shifted to Manasvi Hospital, Nelamangala, but the deceased was died on 06- 12-2022.

10. In order to prove the petition averments, the petitioner no.1 who is the mother in law of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 10 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.8 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, Inquest report, 133 notice and reply, IMV report,
PM report, charge sheet are the material documents to prove the present point.

11. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Hanumanthaiah, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No 0533/2022 of Kudur Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 304(A) IPC.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 338,
304(A) of IPC.
12.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has submitted that since the accident in question has occurred while the deceased was crossing the road and the accident in question has occurred in the middle of the road, the deceased too has contributed negligence hence the petitioners have to forgo compensation to the extent of negligence contributed by the deceased.
The learned counsel at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in ILR 2003 Kar 1104 between Koosappa Poojari Vs. K Sadabba & Ors.,

entities.text: Koosappa Poojari Vs. K Sadabba & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, claimant had crossed the road where he was not supposed to cross.
It was held that certain degree of contributed negligence will have to be attributed him.
If a pedestrian is crossing over a roadway at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing, he cannot claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for causing the accident.
Pedestrian has to share the negligence along with the driver.

Lakshmamma vs Ganesh M.R on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146277636/
3 13.
Coming to the case in hand, admittedly petitioner no.1 who is examined as PW.1 is not an eye witness to the accident.

Though the PW.1 who is not an eye witness to the accident during her cross examination has admitted the suggestion that the accident in question has occurred while the deceased was crossing the road and that the spot of accident is in the middle of the road but if the spot mahazar and rough sketch which is an admitted document is carefully perused, the accident] in question has occurred in Bangalore -Tumkur National High way.
There is service road on both sides of National High way.
The National Highway is of the width of 25 feet each and there is divider in between the road.
If the spot mahazar is perused, the deceased was standing by the side of National Highway leads to Bangalore - Kunigal
. The sketch produced by the petitioners clearly reveals that the deceased has not stepped into the road but she was standing by the side of the road so as to cross the road.
When deceased has not stepped in to the National High way it cannot be said that deceased too has contributed negligence.

When the width of the road is nearly 25 feet the rider of the motorcycle ought not to have ride his vehicle on the extreme left edge of Bangalore - Kunigal road so as to hit against the deceased who as pedestrian was standing on the extreme left edge of the road.
Hence, it can be said that the rider of offending vehicle alone has contributed negligence.
Hence, only the investigating officer after investigation has rightly filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue no 3 :
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioner, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
The respondent no .2 during the course of argument has vehemently submitted that the petitioner no.1 being the mother in law of the deceased is not the legal representative/dependent of the deceased.
Hence, she is not entitled for compensation.

15. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, if the materials placed on record more particularly the evidence of PW.1 is perused, it is not in dispute that petitioner no.1 is the mother in law of the deceased and petitioner no.2 is the minor son of deceased.
The husband of deceased predeceased the deceased.

Though the petitioner no.1 has deposed that after the death of her son i.e., the husband of deceased, herself, deceased and petitioner no.2 were residing together, but if the complaint lodged by the brother of the deceased is perused, wherein he has stated that after the death of the husband of deceased, she is residing with her son in the maternal house of the deceased.

Even if it is taken for a while for the sake of discussion that petitioner no.1 was residing with the deceased and petitioner no.2 but petitioner no.1 being the mother in law of the deceased she cannot claim that she is the legal representative of the deceased or that she is the dependent of the deceased.
Hence, it can be said that petitioner no.1 is not the legal representative and dependent of the deceased and she is not entitled for compensation.

She being the guardian of the petitioner no.2 is entitled to represent the petitioner no.2.
16.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 25 years.
In this regard, the petitioners have produced Ex.P10/Aadhaar card of the deceased where in her date of birth is mentioned as 09-04-1997.
Hence as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 25 years.

Lakshmamma vs Ganesh M.R on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146277636/
4 17.

sentences.text:
So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was doing a tailoring work in Gokul Garments, Bangalore, thereby earning Rs.20,000/-
p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.

18. It is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that the deceased was working in Gokul Das Garments and earning sum of Rs.8,985/- per month and petitioners intentionally have suppressed the pay slip of the deceased, hence submitted to consider the income of the deceased as provided under minimum wages Act.
19. If Ex.R1 coupled with the evidence of PW.1 and the petition averments is perused, it is not in dispute that deceased was working in Gokul Garments.
It is relevant to state here that the respondent no.2 has taken steps to summon the employer of deceased to produce the pay slip of the deceased.

Though this court has allowed the said application filed by the respondent no.2 and summons was issued to the employer of the deceased but since the petitioners have made representation that they will produced the pay slip of the deceased to prove her income, the respondent no.2 did not proceed to take further steps.
The petitioners having submitted that they will produce the pay slip of the deceased but at later stage submitted that they have no document pertaining to the pay slip of the deceased.

Subsequently the learned counsel for respondent no.2 has not proceeded to take steps to summon the pay slip of the deceased from the Gokul Garments instead the learned counsel for respondent no.2 submitted that they have no oral evidence to lead.

Hence, the petitioners have not proved the income of the deceased to say that deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month and at the same time the respondent no.2 has failed to prove that the monthly income of the deceased was Rs.8,985/-.
20.
The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at this juncture has referred the judgment rendered in SLP 3511/2020 between Hans Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd.

entities.text: Hans Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, it was observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that "the guidelines issued from time to time by the State Legal Services Authority were to ordinarily apply where the proof of earning is not available and to settle such disputes in Lok Adalat.

It is also required to be observed that such guidelines ought not to be made applicable for determining just and reasonable compensation in the cases where the proof of earning has been brought on record.

In the facts of this case, we have no hesitation to conclude that the High Court had misdirected itself while reducing the amount of compensation relying upon the guidelines of Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority, which were not binding on them".

"In view of the foregoing, it is to conclude that henceforth, the guidelines, if any,
issued by any of the State Legal Services Authority of the High Court would apply as guiding factor in the cases where the proof of income is not available and ordinarily to decide the cases the Lok Adalat.
Such guidelines are not binding either on the High court or on MACT to determine just and fair compensation.
The Courts are at liberty to decide the amount of compensation while appreciating the evidence so brought on record and what is just and reasonable in the facts.
In absence of such evidence, the guidelines of the legal services authority may be relied upon but for guidance".

Lakshmamma vs Ganesh M.R on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146277636/
5 21.

In MFA No.7404/2014 between Smt. Mariyamma & Ors., Sri Suyambulingam V & Anr., wherein it was observed that "the Minimum Wages Act prescribed a method under which the income of a skilled, unskilled, semiskilled and skilled worker can be considered.
It acts as a basis for various other purpose and even under the Workmen's Compensation Act.

Therefore, the notional income of a deceased who did not have a valid proof of income can very well be guided by the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act and it is for the Tribunal to consider whether he was a skilled, unskilled, semiskilled or unskilled labourer.
The range of the wages between highly Tribunal while assessing the income of the deceased.

The wages under the minimum Wages Act serve as the guidance and depending on the educational, economic conditions and age,
the tribunals have to consider the notional income".
22.

In the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court it was clearly observed that in the absence of clear proof regarding the income of the claimant the guidelines of Legal Service Authority may be relied upon.

In the present case since there is no proof as to the monthly income of the deceased,
considering the fact that the accident in question has occurred in the year 2022, the court inclines to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
23.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had son, 50% of the annual income is to be deducted towards he personal expenses and remaining 50% is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
24.

Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case, as deceased was aged around 25 years, 40% should be added towards future prospects.

25. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/-, by adding 40% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.21,700/-, out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.10,850/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.23,46,600/-
(Rs 10,850/- x 18 x 12 =23,43,600/- ).
26.
Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner No.2 had lost his mother.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of Lakshmamma vs Ganesh M.R on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146277636/
6
dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/-
and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

27. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- to the petitioner no 2 under the head loss of parental consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.

28. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioner no.2 due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs.18,150/-
 2 Transportation and funeral  expenses Rs.18,150/-
 3 Loss of parental consortium Rs.48,400/-
 (Rs.48,400)
 4 Loss of Dependency Rs.23,43,600/-

Thus, the petitioner no.2 is entitled to Rs.24,28,300/-
and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
29. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioner no.2.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
30. Issue No.4 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 2 and 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

Lakshmamma vs Ganesh M.R on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146277636/
7
The petitioner no.2 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.24,28,300/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA-III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.24,28,800/- (Rupees Twenty Four Lakh Twenty Eight Thousand Eight Hundred only).
A Sum of Rs.28,28,300/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the amount with interest within 2 months from the date of award.

The entire compensation amount and interest is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 till he attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 7th day of November 2024.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
